text.p: Iran on Tuesday called for Moslems to stop the Israeli "atrocity" in Jerusalem and said the issue of Jewish settlements would top the agenda of Sunday's Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) summit.

Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told reporters in Kuwait: "No Moslem should permit the Israelis to continue their atrocity against" Jerusalem which is holy to Moslems, Jews and Christians.
He said Moslem states plan to confront Israel, which earlier on Tuesday started work on a planned Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Pakistan will on Sunday host a one-day OIC summit to mark its 50th independence anniversary. OIC foreign ministers will meet on Saturday to draft a summit communique.
"I don't think we will have enough time to do everything that we should about the very important and sensitive question, Jerusalem," said Velayati before flying to Qatar.
But, he said: "this issue will have very top priority in our discussion...this is a disaster now that the Moslems are facing."
Jerusalem "is very important for all of us. We can't ignore the importance of this issue," he said in English.
Velayati, on a tour to invite Moslem leaders to an OIC summit in Tehran in December, will this month participate in meetings by the OIC's Jerusalem committee in Morocco.
Velayati said non-Arab Iran was also told that Arab League foreign ministers plan a meeting "in the near future" on Jerusalem.

Iran and some Arab states have strongly criticised the United States for vetoing a United Nations resolution against the Israeli settlement. The draft was backed by the other 14 members of the U.N. Security Council.
